A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FunDPS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are available and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original FunDPS reconstruction, timing and ablation results across five PDE settings, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparative results and a guidance-weight sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The neural-operator denoiser, Gaussian random field noising, joint representation, guided sampler and ReNoise procedure remain. v1 Algorithm 1 reappears as v2 Algorithm 2 in Appendix B; the task-specific weight revision does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The five PDE families and observation scenarios remain. However, v1 Appendix D describes the Navier–Stokes field u as vorticity, whereas v2 Appendix E describes it as velocity and exchanges the velocity/vorticity notation. Retained initial-condition notation, results and illustrations leave unclear whether the evaluated field actually changed or only its description.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 8–9 add DiffusionPDE to resolution and observation-sparsity comparisons previously reporting FunDPS configurations alone in v1 Table 7 and Figure 7. The main baseline set and the DPS/DDNM/DAPS comparison in Table 5 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes the Poisson inverse PDE-loss weight from 10 to 0. Added evaluations include guidance weights from 1,000 to 50,000 at 500 sampling steps, 500/2,000-step DiffusionPDE comparisons, and a stated 20,000-step DAPS check. These disclosures do not establish that the retained headline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a guidance-weight sensitivity and divergence study on Darcy and Poisson problems (H.6, Table 10). It also extends existing resolution-transfer and observation-count analyses with baseline comparisons (Tables 8–9), while retaining the earlier component and boundary-condition ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose averaging inference timing over 10 runs. v2 introduces no new seed information, uncertainty intervals, significance tests or repeated-accuracy-run reporting; the additional tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and matched existing tables and figures retain their numerical entries. New results include 35.57% error for DiffusionPDE versus 3.64% for FunDPS at 500 steps under 64-to-128 resolution transfer (v2 Table 8), sparsity comparisons, and guidance-induced divergence. H.1 additionally reports that 20,000-step DAPS can match DPS accuracy at 100 times the runtime.

T1.justification: Equation 13 corrects the likelihood-gradient coefficient from c^2/2 to c/2, consistent with the stated covariance approximation. The Banach-space Tweedie theorem moves from v1 Theorem B.6 to v2 Theorem 3.1 with the same assumptions and proof; that relocation is not new theory.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the function-space Tweedie extension, discretization-independent conditional sampling, multi-resolution efficiency and the 32% headline performance advantage. Added speedup wording in the abstract reiterates claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds a high-noise limitation of the likelihood approximation in Section 3.3. H.1 explains DDNM's weak sparse-measurement projections and DAPS's discontinuous intermediate updates; H.6 explains insufficient guidance at low weights and instability at high weights.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the explicit Helmholtz coefficient-generation recipe with a citation and removes the Navier–Stokes statement specifying 10 timesteps. It adds an explicit 128×128 resolution and twofold-downsampling statement and revises Table 4's guidance setting. Architecture, hardware and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cardoso et al.'s Monte Carlo guided diffusion work and Rout et al.'s latent-diffusion posterior-sampling work. These support the approximation caveat and discussion of Tweedie-based guidance; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized contribution and method rewrites, terminology changes from mixed-resolution to multi-resolution, and affiliation/header updates. The formal theorem moves into the main text, sampler pseudocode moves to Appendix B, and qualitative comparisons move to Appendix K; the overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–10 and moves/resizes v1's ReNoise Figure 6 as main-text Figure 4. Existing qualitative figures are retained and relocated, while table captions and pseudocode layouts are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons and guidance-weight ablation strengthen evidence about resolution transfer, sparse observations and sampling failures. The high-noise qualification and Equation 13 correction improve precision. These limited gains are partly offset by reduced dataset-generation detail and the unresolved Navier–Stokes field description; the core method and headline numerical results remain unchanged.
